## The tools

::: {.ce-cards}
::: {.ce-card}
#### [National trends](../national-trends/index.qmd)
The ratio by sector and Carnegie group since 1998, measured or timing-adjusted, as a ratio or as credits per degree; where it exceeds 1; entering vs graduating classes.
:::
::: {.ce-card}
#### [Where the gain came from](../where-the-gain-came-from/index.qmd)
The exact accounting of 2010–22, with a dial for every assumption, and the community-college / university split.
:::
::: {.ce-card}
#### [State explorer](../state-explorer/index.qmd)
Map any state measure, open a state's profile with its policy dates, or plot any two measures against each other.
:::
::: {.ce-card}
#### [Institution explorer](../institution-explorer/index.qmd)
Any college's path, its own entering classes, its peers; the outsourcing split by institution type.
:::
::: {.ce-card}
#### [Price per degree](../price-per-degree/index.qmd)
Tuition per credit vs tuition per degree for the nation, sectors, states and colleges.
:::
::: {.ce-card}
#### [Credit channels](../credit-channels/index.qmd)
AP, dual enrollment, transfer and certificates, including what a given AP score earns at a given college.
:::
::: {.ce-card}
#### [Policy timeline](../policy-timeline/index.qmd)
Ten statewide policies, when each state adopted them, against its community-college ratio.
:::
:::

::: {.ce-note}
**The measure.** The efficiency ratio (ER) is degree credits awarded (120 per bachelor's, 60 per associate degree) divided by credits taught, from IPEDS completions and 12-month credit-hour activity. `T = 120 / ER` is credits taught per bachelor's-degree equivalent. Aggregates are ratios of sums, so large colleges count in proportion to the credits they teach. The **timing-adjusted** ratio removes the mechanical effect of entering classes that are larger or smaller than the classes now graduating, institution by institution. State results are for **public** systems: public universities and community colleges together. Source: white paper v5 (draft, 2026-10-05); IPEDS, College Board, National Student Clearinghouse; author's calculations.
:::
